analysis: The PR changes only documentation: docs/developer/build.md (full head text across three units, with a bumped last-updated stamp) and docs/developer/test.md (a patch that adds a test note on integration-CI workflow invariants and a Docs Impact merge-base note). No source code, authorization logic, attestation logic, encryption or billing paths were modified, so I found no concrete security regression. I did not diff the build.md head text against base because only head text was supplied. The text describes CI cache handling, pinned tool checksums, component-path routing and App Attest build qualification. These are consistent with the existing threat model assumptions (TB-011, T-054 build qualification, T-041 cache posture) and do not contradict them. The T-041 definition was supplied as context, and the build.md statements about SSD cache opt-in and ephemeral storage do not alter its posture. Test.md:0 was a metadata-only unit with no patch text; I treated it as examined but with no visible content. Coverage limit: unchanged code was not reviewed, and the documented CI behaviors (cache restore, merge-base detection) were not verified against actual scripts or workflows.
